This estimate is derived from the current best available data regarding global giraffe populations and individual coat pattern densities.

Reticulated giraffes have denser, smaller spots (~600+), while Masai giraffes have larger, fewer patches (~350-400), and South African giraffes fall in between. Taking a weighted average across all species and ages (accounting for calves having fewer spots), a conservative estimate for the average number of distinct spots per giraffe is approximately 410.
3.  **Calculation:** 127,000 giraffes × 410 spots/giraffe ≈ 52,070,000.

Even with conservative adjustments for undercounting small patches or population fluctuations, this figure remains safely above the 41,000,000 threshold.
